frontier.hypothesis: The callee-saved permutation (the s2/s3 rotation plus the temp_s4/temp_s5 assignment - together ~13 of the remaining 28 diffs) flips on REG_N_REFS, and the decisive pair is pseudo 73 (arg1 home, 7 refs / 92 insns, pri 1521) against pseudo 75 (temp_s4, 6 refs / 88 insns, pri 1363), which are adjacent in the priority order.
frontier.mechanism: flow.c weights REG_N_REFS by loop_depth and global.c:635-655 allocno_compare sorts by pri = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*10000*size/live_length with an ascending-allocno tiebreak; MIPS defines no REG_ALLOC_ORDER so find_reg walks hard regs ascending and the first-allocated call-crossing pseudo takes the lowest free callee-saved register. The do-while experiment proved the order moves on n_refs alone with every live length pinned.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate ORDINARY-C restructures that legitimately change one of those two reference counts by exactly one, and re-dump .lreg after each to confirm the printed ref count actually moved BEFORE reading the score. Strongest candidates: (a) re-read `*(u8 **)(arg0)` at one of the later temp_s4 use sites instead of keeping the hoisted local live - this drops a reference from pseudo 75 and adds one to pseudo 72, and is exactly the kind of thing the original author may have written; (b) the mirror - fold one existing temp_s4 use into an arg0-relative access. Do NOT chase live_length windows: sessions 2 and 3 spent that axis (H9, H9a, and six byte-neutral declaration-order variants).

frontier.hypothesis: Diamond 2's last 8 diffs need BOTH selection copies in target's canonical `v=0x19; if(!s1) v=0xB;` order AND unmerged, which under the traced mechanism means the jump2 pairing must never be ATTEMPTED rather than fail its comparison.
frontier.mechanism: jump.c:2012-2021 - the chain-partner loop is guarded by `if (INSN_UID (JUMP_LABEL (insn)) < max_uid)` and walks jump_chain[] stopping at the first WIN; jump_chain is only populated for jumps whose UID and label UID are below max_jump_chain, so a jump or label CREATED during jump optimization is invisible to the chain.
frontier.next_probe: Unchanged from s3 and still untried: run tmp/grind/func_800283D0/s2/xjump.sh on the CANONICAL both-copies-identical body with the trace instrumented to also print INSN_UID(JUMP_LABEL) and max_uid, and check whether block_48's label UID is below max_uid at all. If it is, enumerate which partners are tried for e1 and in what order, and look for a statement placement earlier in the function that gives e1 an EARLIER chain partner that wins first (a byte-neutral merge elsewhere). Both 'make the copies structurally different at the jump' routes are dead (s2 distinct terminator, s3 two-goto labels, s3 ternary).

frontier.hypothesis: The tail a0/a1 cluster flips when the temp_a0 quantity's local-alloc priority reaches a TIE with the Judge[] element's, i.e. span(qty0) <= 24 (3 fewer insns, from 30) or span(qty3) >= 6 (one more insn between the `lh Judge` and the `mult`).
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c qty_compare_1 pri = floor_log2(n_refs)*n_refs*size/(death-birth)*10000, ties -> ascending qty number, and qty0 (pointer, combined with the sll producer and var_a1) < qty3 (Judge[] element).
frontier.next_probe: Unchanged from s3: the declaration-order axis and the combine_regs attack are both KILLED, so the remaining honest axes are (a) raise qty3's span from 4 to >=6 by getting one more insn scheduled between the `lh Judge(at)` and its `mult` - a sched1 question, so read tmp/grind/func_800283D0/dumps/code6cac_b.sched for block 41's ready-list ordering FIRST - or (b) shrink qty0's span to <=24 by making the `lw 0x118` land 3 insns earlier at local-alloc time. Note the s4 finding that the CALLEE-saved permutation is ref-count-driven does not transfer here: this cluster is caller-saved and local-alloc, a different sorter.
